title: Relative flat bar computes sheaf dg extension with its action counit
statement:
Let $D$ be a commutative ring, $X$ a topological space, and $\mathcal S$ a sheaf of commutative $D$-algebras. Let $\varphi:P\to Q$ be a map of associative unital dg $D$-algebras [def-sfb-dg-derived-category], and suppose their underlying $D$-complexes are K-flat [def-pc-module-kflat-complex]. Write $\mathcal C=\mathcal S\otimes_D P$ and $\mathcal C'=\mathcal S\otimes_D Q$, with sheafification of the tensor understood. Use the left sheaf dg module localizations and derived extension notation of [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. Then derived extension along $\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ exists and is left adjoint to restriction. For every possibly unbounded sheaf dg $\mathcal C$-module $M$, its value is represented by the $D$-relative two-sided bar complex
$$B(Q,P,M)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}V_n[n],\qquad V_n=Q\otimes_D P^{\otimes_D n}\otimes_D M.$$
All tensors are tensor products of sheaves, and internal tensor differentials use the direct-sum total convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. On $V_n[n]$, the internal differential is $(-1)^n d_{V_n}$ and the other component is $\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i\partial_i$ into $V_{n-1}[n-1]$ for $n>0$. From left to right the faces multiply $Q$ by $P$ through $\varphi$, multiply adjacent $P$ factors, and act on $M$; degeneracies insert units. The $\mathcal S$-action is retained on $M$. The left $Q$-action on the summand $V_n[n]$ includes the factor $(-1)^{n|q|}$ for a homogeneous $q\in Q$.

This bar construction preserves quasi-isomorphisms of $M$ and is natural in its derived-category morphisms. Its comparison to ordinary extension is the balanced quotient on $V_0$ and zero on $V_n[n]$ for $n>0$. For a sheaf dg $\mathcal C'$-module $N$, the adjunction counit is represented by $B(Q,P,\operatorname{Res}N)\to N$ which is $q\otimes n\mapsto qn$ on $V_0$ and zero on higher bar summands. In particular the counit retains the given $\mathcal S$-action. For $P=D$, there is a natural identification of this derived extension with $(\mathcal S\otimes_D Q)\otimes_{\mathcal S}^{\mathbf L}-$ in the corresponding dg module category, whose underlying object is $Q\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}M$. No flatness of $\mathcal S$ over $D$ or of the underlying complex of $M$ over $D$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply the general sheaf dg scalar adjunction on the open site of $X$, with base $\mathcal S$, to $\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$, passing to opposite algebras for left modules. It gives the unbounded universal derived extension $L$, its comparison $\varepsilon_M:L(M)\to F(M)$ for $F(M)=\mathcal C'\otimes_{\mathcal C}M$, and the adjunction to restriction whose counit is comparison followed by action. Thus it remains to identify this specified derived pair with the displayed bar and its augmentation; no new adjunction is chosen.

source.place: Tags 0FTF, 0FTR, identity underlying topos; left version by opposites.

proof.text: Construct $B(M)$ with the faces, degeneracies and total differential in the statement. Put $\delta_n=\sum_i(-1)^i\partial_i$. Associativity and the module law give $\partial_i\partial_j=\partial_{j-1}\partial_i$ for $i<j$, hence $\delta_{n-1}\delta_n=0$ by cancelling pairs; each face is an internal chain map, so $(-1)^{n-1}d\delta_n+\delta_n(-1)^nd=0$. Thus $D^2=0$. The shifted action $q\cdot v=(-1)^{n|q|}qv$ satisfies Leibniz internally. Horizontally, $\delta(q\cdot v)=(-1)^{|q|}q\cdot\delta(v)$, since the source and target actions have exponents $n|q|$ and $(n-1)|q|$. The degree-zero $\mathcal S$-action on $M$ commutes with all these maps. This defines a sheaf dg $\mathcal C'$-module without a flatness assumption.

source.place: Agent bar sign calculation using the left conventions of section-shift and section-tensor-product-dg.

proof.text: The quotient map $\alpha_M:B(M)\to F(M)$ on length zero, zero elsewhere, is a chain map: on length one the two faces become the same balanced tensor, so their difference vanishes. It is $\mathcal C'$-linear. Module maps act on the last factor, naturally commuting with $\alpha$. A degree $-1$ module homotopy $h$ induces $H_n=(-1)^n(1\otimes h)$ on length $n$, with the usual tensor Koszul sign in $1\otimes h$. The internal terms of $DH+HD$ give the induced difference of maps; the horizontal terms cancel because $\delta$ commutes with $1\otimes h$ and $H_n$ has alternating sign. Consequently $B$ and $\alpha$ descend to the homotopy categories.

source.place: Agent chain calculation; tensor signs from section-tensor-product-dg.

proof.text: At a point of $X$, the constant complex associated with $P$ (respectively $Q$) has stalk $P$ (respectively $Q$), by evaluating a locally constant germ at the point (inverse: the constant germ); apply the stalk K-flatness criterion. Thus these constant sheaf complexes are K-flat over the constant ring sheaf $D_X$. Finite tensor products are K-flat directly from the definition: tensor with an acyclic complex successively, using associativity of the direct-sum tensor. Therefore $Q\otimes_D P^{\otimes n}\otimes_D A$ is acyclic for every acyclic sheaf complex $A$. Stalk tensor comparison ensures these are precisely the sheafified tensors in the statement, not tensors over $\mathcal S$.

source.place: K-flat tensor criterion on the constant ringed space; sdga relative bar refinement is agent-written.

proof.text: For a quasi-isomorphism $f:M\to M'$, filter the mapping cone of $B(f)$ by bar lengths $0\le n\le r$. This is an increasing filtration by subcomplexes, because faces lower length. Its $r$th quotient is the shifted cone of $1\otimes f$ on $Q\otimes_D P^{\otimes r}\otimes_D M$; it is acyclic by the preceding step. Starting with the zero stage, the long exact cohomology sequence for the degreewise split filtration sequence proves each finite stage acyclic. The full cone is the filtered colimit of these stages. Filtered colimits of abelian sheaves are exact, so commute with kernels, images and cohomology; hence the full cone is acyclic. Thus $B$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, even for unbounded $M$, and induces $\overline B:D_X(\mathcal C)\to D_X(\mathcal C')$.

source.place: Agent increasing-length proof; derived tensor localization as in Tag 0FTF.

proof.text:
Let $R=B(Q,P,\mathcal C)$, with its additional right $\mathcal C$-action on the last factor. Its augmentation $u:R\to\mathcal C'$ multiplies the two algebra factors on length zero and is zero above it. As a complex of $\mathcal S$-modules it retracts onto $\mathcal C'$: $i(s\otimes q)=q\otimes(s\otimes1)$ and, on length $n\ge0$,
$$h_n(q\otimes p_1\otimes\cdots\otimes p_n\otimes(s\otimes p))=(-1)^{n+1}q\otimes p_1\otimes\cdots\otimes p_n\otimes p\otimes(s\otimes1).$$
The last face contributes the identity; each other face cancels the matching term in $h\delta$. In length zero the remaining term is $-iu$. Internal differentials anticommute with $h$ because it increases length and commutes with the unshifted tensor differential. Thus $Dh+hD=1-iu$ and $ui=1$. In particular $u$ is a quasi-isomorphism of right dg $\mathcal C$-modules. The contraction need not be right $\mathcal C$-linear.

source.place: Agent explicit extra-degeneracy contraction; no flatness of S is used.

proof.text:
Choose $h:H\to M$ with $H$ graded-flat and homotopically flat over $\mathcal C$ by the sheaf dg resolution theorem. Its comparison $\varepsilon_H:L(H)\to F(H)$ is invertible. Homotopical flatness means $u\otimes_{\mathcal C}H$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Balancing gives the chain isomorphism
$$R\otimes_{\mathcal C}H\cong B(Q,P,H),\qquad (q\otimes\mathbf p\otimes c)\otimes m\longmapsto q\otimes\mathbf p\otimes cm,$$
with inverse inserting $c=1$. The total differential and both actions agree termwise; in particular no sign is introduced by shifting the first tensor factor with the right-module convention. Under this map $u\otimes H$ is exactly $\alpha_H$, so $\alpha_H$ is a quasi-isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0FSH and 0FTF for the resolving computation; agent balancing of the displayed bar.

proof.text: The universal property of the left derived pair $(L,\varepsilon)$ applied to $\alpha:\overline B\,Q_{\mathcal C}\to Q_{\mathcal C'}F$ gives $\beta:\overline B\to L$ with $\varepsilon\beta=\alpha$. On the resolving $H$ of the preceding step, both $\varepsilon_H$ and $\alpha_H$ are invertible, so $\beta_H$ is invertible. Naturality along $h:H\to M$ then makes $\beta_M$ invertible: both $L(h)$ and $\overline B(h)$ are isomorphisms. This proves the bar represents the specified universal derived extension, naturally for every localized morphism, with its specified comparison $\alpha$. The inherited adjunction counit is consequently $\alpha_{\operatorname{Res}N}$ followed by ordinary action. It is $q\otimes n\mapsto qn$ on length zero and zero above it, and is $\mathcal S$-linear.

source.place: Universal left-derived comparison and action counit of Tags 0FTF and 0FTR; elementary universal-property argument.

proof.text: For $P=D$, identify every unshifted $V_n$ with $Q\otimes_D M$ by multiplying the scalar $D$-factors. Every face becomes the identity, so $\delta_n$ is the identity for positive even $n$ and zero for odd $n$. The augmentation onto length zero has a contraction on its positive-length kernel: take $h_n$ to be the identity into length $n+1$ for odd $n$ and zero for even $n$. Then $\delta h+h\delta=1$ there and the internal terms cancel by the alternating shift sign. It follows that $B(Q,D,M)\to Q\otimes_D M$ is a natural quasi-isomorphism of $\mathcal C'$-modules. Ordinary balancing identifies the target with $(\mathcal S\otimes_D Q)\otimes_{\mathcal S}M$. The preceding derived-pair identification gives exactly the asserted derived extension over $\mathcal S$.

source.place: Agent unit-algebra contraction; K-flat computation of ordinary derived tensor.

proof.text: For completeness, the underlying derived tensor needs no flat terms on $Q$. For the constant ring sheaf $D_X$, choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $T\to Q_X$. Its cone is acyclic and K-flat (tensoring its cone with any acyclic complex gives the cone of a map between acyclic tensor complexes). The acyclic K-flat tensor lemma makes $T\otimes_D M\to Q_X\otimes_D M$ a quasi-isomorphism for arbitrary unbounded $M$. The one-sided site tensor comparison identifies $T\otimes_D M$ with $Q_X\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}M$, since $T\simeq Q_X$. These maps retain the $\mathcal S$-action on the last factor. If desired, take $T$ to be the constant realization of a flat-term K-flat $D$-module resolution of $Q$, so all comparisons visibly have this action. Thus the underlying bar value for $P=D$ is the asserted $Q\otimes_D^{\mathbf L}M$.
